question: Can GoalAnchor enforce tool gating on ZCode without installing a host plugin?

host.name: ZCode Desktop
host.version: 3.16.3 desktop; embedded CLI bundle at D:\AIWorkspace\Tools\ZCode\resources\glm\zcode.cjs (15.7 MB)

experiment_1_app_server_permission_callb.method: scripts/zcode_permission_probe.py subclasses the existing ProbeClient and, instead of denying every host interaction, records interaction/requestPermission and answers 'allow' so a tool call can proceed. A prompt asking for a Bash call was sent over the app-server NDJSON protocol with provider=magpie, model=auto/deepseek-v4.1-flash, reasoningLevel=medium, mode=build.

result.response_text_excerpt: <｜｜DSML｜｜ calls> <｜｜DSML｜｜ invoke name="Bash"> <｜｜DSML｜｜ parameter name="command" string="true">echo ZCODE_PERM_PROBE</｜｜DSML｜｜ parameter> ... </｜｜DSML｜｜ calls>
result.interpretation: Over the CLI/app-server path the model emits tool calls as DSML TEXT in the assistant message; the host does not execute them and therefore never raises a permission request. tool_call_count is 0 and no tool frame appears.

experiment_1_app_server_permission_callb.conclusion: The app-server path cannot host a pre-execution approval gate: there is no tool execution, hence no permission callback to answer.

experiment_2_native_permission_mode.method: Read the ZCode desktop UI accessibility tree for the permission control.
experiment_2_native_permission_mode.result: The composer exposes a native permission-mode control labelled '完全访问' (full access) next to '电脑操作', and the app-server protocol exposes mode settings ('plan'/'build') plus session permission.scope=session. The protocol callback 'interaction/requestPermission' is implemented by the host and the existing probe answers it with deny.
experiment_2_native_permission_mode.interpretation: The host DOES have a native pre-tool approval gate, but it lives inside the desktop host's own execution path. A client that only speaks the CLI/app-server protocol cannot intercept it; only the desktop host itself raises it.
experiment_2_native_permission_mode.conclusion: Zero-plugin enforcement would require the host to route its approval decision to an external party (an MCP server or a plugin), not merely to the user.

host_mcp_surface.evidence: ZCode's own bundle (resources/glm/zcode.cjs) implements MCP support: a plugin-root '.mcp.json' file, a 'mcpServers' key honoured at user / project / local scope, and an agent-frontmatter 'mcpServers' list ('Agent frontmatter mcpServers must be a list of parent server names'). The host ships the official 'zcode-mcp-app-dev' plugin and keeps mcp-oauth lock files.
host_mcp_surface.implication: GoalAnchor could be published as a STANDARD MCP server (stdio), registered by .mcp.json or an agent frontmatter, exposing its gate/review tools to the host. MCP is a published protocol rather than a private host API, so a host upgrade is far less likely to break it than a plugin.
host_mcp_surface.not_yet_done: No MCP server implementation exists in the repository yet, and no ZCode MCP registration has been performed or verified.

verdict: ZCODE_ENFORCEMENT_WITHOUT_PLUGIN_POSSIBLE_VIA_MCP_NOT_YET_BUILT: the CLI/app-server path has no tool execution and therefore no permission callback to hook; the desktop host has a native approval gate but it is internal; the standards-based route is to publish GoalAnchor as an MCP server and let the host call it. The Skill + CLI protocol layer is already verified on this host (PR #48).
reproduce: python scripts/zcode_permission_probe.py --output <new json> --workspace <dir> --prompt 'Use the Bash tool to run exactly: echo ZCODE_PERM_PROBE. Then report the output.'
